ic_name: MIPI D-PHY / CSI-2 (TI SLLA414 application note)
signaling_summary: Pure digital synchronous-serial peripheral; CMOS-level single-ended signals on the named external pins; sampling/shift edges determined by clock polarity/phase configuration; clock generated by master baud-rate generator from BusClock divisor.
analog_components_per_lane: HS differential receiver with 100 Ω internal differential termination + threshold comparator
LP push-pull CMOS driver (1.2 V rail-to-rail)
LP receiver — two single-ended CMOS Schmitt inputs (one per Dp, one per Dn)
Lane-state controller — selects HS vs LP driver/receiver based on lane state
notes: Although CSI-2 protocol is purely digital, D-PHY is firmly mixed-signal: the HS driver is current-mode at multi-gigabit and requires careful analog design (output impedance, common-mode, jitter). The LP path is standard CMOS but must coexist with the HS path on the same pins. The lane-state controller arbitrates the two.
